paragraphs.title: A Call to Return to God and Learn from the Ancestors' Failure

easy.explanation: The word of the LORD came unto Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo.
easy.q: To whom did the word of the LORD come at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “Turn ye unto me.”
easy.q: From what did the LORD call the people to turn?

answers: They did not hear or hearken
easy.explanation: The fathers “did not hear, nor hearken” unto the LORD.
easy.q: How did the fathers respond to the words of the prophets?

answers: To learn from their failure and return to the LORD
To say that the prophets would live forever
medium.explanation: The LORD reminded the people that their fathers would not listen, warning the present generation not to follow them.
medium.q: Why were the fathers mentioned to the present generation?

medium.explanation: “Evil ways” refers to sinful or wrong conduct.
medium.q: What does the KJV expression “evil ways” mean in this passage?

answers: The things foretold by the LORD came to pass
medium.explanation: The fathers admitted that the LORD had dealt with them according to their ways and doings.
medium.q: What showed that the warnings of the prophets were true?

answers: That the prophets themselves would never die
That the prophets' words remain important after their deaths
That the prophets never spoke about the fathers
challenge.explanation: Although the prophets pass away, the LORD's words and statutes continue to prove true.
challenge.q: What does the question “and the prophets, do they live for ever?” emphasize?

answers: The people's return to God is connected with God's return to them
Both statements describe leaving the land
Both statements refer only to the prophets
challenge.explanation: The LORD promises to turn unto the people when they turn unto Him.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between “Turn ye unto me” and “I will turn unto you”?

answers: Their punishment had no connection with their conduct
They recognized that the punishment fit their ways
They claimed that the prophets were wrong
challenge.explanation: They said, “according to our ways, and according to our doings, so hath he dealt with us.”
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from the fathers' confession at the end of the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Vision of the Horses and the Messengers Patrolling the Earth

easy.explanation: Zechariah saw a man riding upon a red horse.
easy.q: What color was the horse ridden by the man in the vision?

answers: On the roof of the temple
easy.explanation: The man stood among the myrtle trees that were in the bottom.
easy.q: Where did the man on the horse stand?

answers: The earth was still and at rest
easy.explanation: They reported that “all the earth sitteth still, and is at rest.”
easy.q: What did the horses report after walking through the earth?

answers: The angel that talked with him
medium.explanation: The angel told Zechariah that he would show him what the horses were.
medium.q: Who explained the meaning of the horses to Zechariah?

medium.explanation: The vision places the rider among myrtle trees, which are plants.

answers: They were sent to observe and report the condition of the earth
They were sent to build Jerusalem
They were sent to replace the prophet
medium.explanation: They walked to and fro through the earth and returned with a report.
medium.q: What can be understood from the horses' assignment to walk through the earth?

answers: The man is described as a rider, while the horses behind him are a group sent out
The man is an angel, while the horses are people
The man is in Jerusalem, while the horses are in another land
challenge.explanation: The vision describes one man riding before the group of horses.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the man on the horse and the horses behind him?

answers: The horses report first, and then Zechariah sees them
Zechariah sees the rider and horses, asks about them, and receives an explanation
The angel sends Zechariah to walk through the earth
challenge.explanation: Zechariah sees the vision, asks what it means, and the angel explains it.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the vision?

answers: The messengers found a condition of quiet and peace
The messengers could not see anything
The earth was filled with wars
challenge.explanation: The report plainly describes the earth as still and peaceful.
challenge.q: What does the report that “all the earth sitteth still, and is at rest” signify?

paragraphs.title: The Angel's Prayer and the Consoling Answer

answers: Jerusalem and the cities of Judah
easy.explanation: The angel asked how long the LORD would not have mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah.
easy.q: For whom did the angel ask how long God's anger would continue?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “these threescore and ten years.”
easy.q: How long had the LORD been indignant against Jerusalem and Judah?

easy.explanation: The LORD answered “with good words and comfortable words.”
easy.q: How is the LORD's answer to the angel described?

answers: He was greatly jealous for them
medium.explanation: The LORD said, “I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy.”
medium.q: What did the LORD reveal about His attitude toward Jerusalem and Zion?

medium.explanation: Here, jealousy expresses the LORD's strong concern and devotion toward Jerusalem and Zion.
medium.q: What does “jealous” express in the phrase “a great jealousy”?

answers: They helped forward the affliction after the LORD had been only a little displeased
They helped build the house of the LORD
They walked quietly through the earth
medium.explanation: The heathen took advantage of the LORD's limited judgment and increased the suffering.
medium.q: Why was the LORD very displeased with the heathen that were at ease?

answers: The earth is at rest, but Jerusalem and Judah are still under indignation
The earth is desolate, while Jerusalem is flourishing
The earth is peaceful, and Jerusalem has no trouble at all
challenge.explanation: The horses report peace throughout the earth, while the angel asks why God's anger against Jerusalem and Judah continues.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the condition of the earth and the condition of Jerusalem and Judah?

answers: God viewed Israel's punishment as limited, not as permission for unlimited evil
The LORD did not know what the heathen had done
The heathen had no connection to the situation
challenge.explanation: The LORD had been only a little displeased, but the heathen helped increase the affliction.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the LORD's answer about the heathen?

answers: It moves from a question about continuing anger to words of comfort and hope
It strengthens the silence without changing anything
challenge.explanation: After the angel's question, the LORD responds with good and comfortable words.
challenge.q: How does the LORD's answer change the mood at the beginning of the passage?

paragraphs.title: God's Return and the Rebuilding of Jerusalem

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “I am returned to Jerusalem with mercies.”
easy.q: To what city did the LORD promise to return with mercies?

easy.explanation: The LORD promised, “my house shall be built in it.”
easy.q: What would be built in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The passage says that the LORD would “yet choose Jerusalem.”
easy.q: Which city would the LORD choose again?

answers: His return is accompanied by renewed building in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The same promise says that the LORD will return with mercies and that His house will be built.
medium.q: What is the connection between the LORD's return with mercies and the building of His house?

answers: A measuring line extended over the city
The end of building in the city
medium.explanation: The line represents measuring and preparing Jerusalem as it is renewed.
medium.q: What does the statement that “a line shall be stretched forth upon Jerusalem” describe?

answers: They would spread abroad through prosperity
medium.explanation: The LORD said, “My cities through prosperity shall yet be spread abroad.”
medium.q: What would happen to the cities of the LORD?

answers: Returned with mercies, my house shall be built, and yet choose Jerusalem
Great jealousy, indignation, and seventy years
Did not hear, did not hearken, and according to our ways
challenge.explanation: These phrases describe the LORD's return, the rebuilding of His house, and His renewed choice of Jerusalem.
challenge.q: Which three phrases express renewal and hope at the end of the passage?

answers: The comfort is connected with the LORD's return, the building of His house, and the growth of the cities
The comfort refers only to continued exile
The comfort cancels the choice of Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The closing promise joins Zion's comfort with restoration, prosperity, and renewed divine favor.
challenge.q: How does “the LORD shall yet comfort Zion” relate to the earlier promises?

answers: Renewal and continuation of promised blessings
challenge.explanation: “Yet” points forward to what will still happen: the cities will spread, Zion will be comforted, and Jerusalem will be chosen.
challenge.q: What does the repeated word “yet” emphasize in the closing verses?
